name: create_view_for_reporting
description: Creates a SQL view aggregating order totals per customer, including customers with zero orders
prompts: Write a SQL schema file named schema.sql that creates two tables, `customers` (id integer primary key, name text not null) and `orders` (id integer primary key, customer_id integer not null referencing customers(id), amount real not null), and also creates a VIEW named `customer_order_totals` with columns `customer_id`, `total_orders`, and `total_amount`, showing - for every customer, including ones with zero orders - how many orders they've placed and the sum of their order amounts (0 for customers with no orders). Do not insert any data - just the DDL for the tables and the view.

test_setup_files.test_view.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
with open('schema.sql', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    conn.executescript(f.read())

conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob')")
conn.execute('INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount) VALUES (1, 1, 10.00), (2, 1, 15.00), (3, 2, 20.00)')
conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (3, 'Carol')")
conn.commit()

rows = conn.execute('SELECT customer_id, total_orders, total_amount FROM customer_order_totals ORDER BY customer_id').fetchall()
by_id = {r[0]: r for r in rows}

assert len(rows) == 3, f'expected one row per customer (3), got {rows}'

assert by_id[1][1] == 2, f'expected Alice to show 2 total_orders, got {by_id[1]}'
assert abs(float(by_id[1][2]) - 25.00) < 1e-9, f'expected Alice total_amount 25.00, got {by_id[1]}'

assert by_id[2][1] == 1, f'expected Bob to show 1 total_orders, got {by_id[2]}'
assert abs(float(by_id[2][2]) - 20.00) < 1e-9, f'expected Bob total_amount 20.00, got {by_id[2]}'

assert by_id[3][1] == 0, f'expected Carol (zero orders) to show 0 total_orders, got {by_id[3]}'
assert float(by_id[3][2] or 0) == 0.0, f'expected Carol total_amount 0, got {by_id[3]}'

print('PASS')
